thesis: A valid experimental program compares full systems under equal resources, structural holdouts, ablations and predefined criteria.

ideas.statement: A valid experimental program compares full systems under equal resources, structural holdouts, ablations and predefined criteria.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Removing diagnosis or consolidation tests their contribution; unseen compositions and total costs can directly refute the intended advantage.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: No zero-error finite test proves perfection; negative findings narrow the claim instead of changing success retrospectively.

audit.notes: Source-grounded analysis; proposed mechanisms and limited guarantees preserved.
